# Stage-2 ELVIS: Preliminary Results

## Implementation

Moment set A (row list authoritative in `Code/Rcpp/1200-stage2-elvis.cpp`'s header comment): $\theta_{\text{smooth}}=(\lambda,\delta_0,\delta_1,\delta_2)$, 9 moments ($d_g=9$), no nuisance parameters beyond $\gamma$:

$$
g(M,Z,\theta_{\text{smooth}})=\begin{pmatrix}
\psi(M,Z) \\
\varepsilon(M,Z) \\
\psi(M,Z)\ln M \\
\psi(M,Z)\omega(M,Z) \\
\psi(M,Z)\omega(M,Z)^2 \\
\varepsilon(M,Z)\ln M \\
\varepsilon(M,Z) e(M,Z) \\
\varepsilon(M,Z)\omega(M,Z) \\
h'(e,\lambda)\,\varepsilon(M,Z)
\end{pmatrix}
$$

## Implementation Details

- **Objective**: CUE quadratic, $\hat L_n(\theta,\gamma)=\tfrac12\hat g'\hat\Omega^-\hat g$, $\hat\Omega^-$ an eigenvalue-truncated generalized inverse — same construction AK2020 use
- **Sampler**: per-firm Metropolis chain, `n_burn=1000, n_keep=3000`, deterministic per-firm RNG reseed
- **Solver**: Nelder-Mead (beats BOBYQA decisively on this problem), unbounded $\gamma$ (a large/degenerate $\gamma$ is an expected solution, Schennach 2014 — not a numerical failure), two-pass refinement
- **Seeding**: every $\lambda$ grid point seeded independently from the same validated starting point — no chaining across grid points

## $\lambda$ Search

- $\lambda$ bounds derived directly from the data: the smallest $\lambda$ for which not even the largest firm's evasion is ever constrained, up to the largest $\lambda$ for which even the smallest firm is constrained
- 16-point log-spaced grid (coarse pass, then a finer pass bracketing the region of interest)
- **Sample**: 32,232 unincorporated firm-periods (3,340 at the $\tau_P=0$ corner), top 0.5% trimmed by $M^*$; two productivity-instrument choices for $(\alpha_K,\alpha_L,\beta)$

## $\hat L_n(\lambda)$ — Both Instruments

![](../Paper/images/1285-lambdagrid-slide.png){height="75%" fig-align="center"}

##

**Reading the picture**:

- $m^*_{it-1}$: a clean V-shape, genuine minimum, real rejection on both sides — a proper confidence interval
- $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$: also rejects everywhere except two points — its own interior minimum, and separately the smallest $\lambda$ we tested. That second pass just means: for this instrument, we can't rule out arbitrarily weak detection either — we only get an upper bound on $\lambda$ from it, not a full interval. Consistent with it being the weaker of the two instruments overall.

## Headline Estimates

| Instrument | $\hat\lambda$ | 95% region | $\hat L_n$ | $\hat\delta_0$ | $\hat\delta_1$ | $\hat\delta_2$ | $\hat\omega^*=\hat\delta_1/2\hat\delta_2$ | $\max\vert\gamma\vert$ |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $m^*_{it-1}$ | $3.50\times10^{-7}$ | $[2.26,5.43]\times10^{-7}$ | 0.000387 | 3.459 | 4.315 | **0.541** | 3.99 | 0.64 |
| $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ | $5.43\times10^{-7}$ | $5.43\times10^{-7}$ (point) | 0.000401 | 10.206 | 7.460 | **0.972** | 3.84 | 1.86 |

$\hat\delta_2>0$ for both — the cost function opens the correct (U-shaped) way. $\hat\omega^*$ lands in a similar plausible range for both, even though the individual $\hat\delta_1,\hat\delta_2$ differ — expected: the two instruments come from different first-stage residuals, so they carry somewhat different implied productivity distributions.

## A Data-Side Check on $\hat\lambda$: What Detection Probability Does This Imply?

Does $\hat\lambda$ imply a sane detection probability at a typical evading firm? Quick check by forward-simulating each firm's own evasion at the fitted $(\hat\theta,\hat\gamma)$ and reading off the population mean/median — **a ballpark reading, not the formal way to pin this down** (that would need its own auxiliary moment, jointly re-estimated with everything else, not a post-hoc average):

| Instrument | $E[e]$ | Med$[e]$ | $q(E[e])=\hat\lambda\cdot E[e]$ | $q(\text{Med}[e])$ |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $m^*_{it-1}$ | 2,545 | 625 | 0.089% | 0.022% |
| $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ | 3,189 | 685 | 0.173% | 0.037% |

- $E[e]\gg\text{Med}[e]$ for both — a right-skewed evasion distribution: most firms evade modestly, a long right tail of aggressive evaders pulls the mean well above the median
- Both implied detection probabilities are small, well under the 50% FOC ceiling — no sign of $\hat\lambda$ pushing anyone near the boundary

## Notes for Discussion

- **$m^*_{it-1}$ is the instrument to lead with**: a genuine, contiguous confidence interval, stable $\hat\delta_1,\hat\delta_2$ across the whole search
- **$\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ confirms the same qualitative story but is the weaker instrument**: real rejection pattern, a real interior optimum, but can only bound $\lambda$ from above, not below
- **No formal joint confidence region for $(\lambda,\delta_1,\delta_2)$ yet** — next step, to get a stronger justification for one fixed $\hat\theta$ to carry into the counterfactual
